meta.name: BackupHelper
meta.description: Windows .NET 9 backup utility that zips local and SMB sources and uploads the archive to filesystem, SMB and Azure Blob destinations.

items.title: Runtime and platform
items.content: Targets .NET 9 and runs on Windows only. Volume shadow copy (AlphaVSS) and the credential store both assume Windows.

items.title: Solution layering
items.content: Layers run: Abstractions (contracts) -> Core (orchestration, zipping, credentials, retention) -> Sources.* and Sinks.* (pluggable transports) -> Connectors.* (vendor SDK wrappers) -> ConsoleApp (wizard, composition root). Dependencies point inward toward Abstractions.

items.title: Test stack
items.content: NUnit as the runner, Shouldly for assertions, shared fakes in the Tests.Shared project. Coverage collected via coverlet.

items.title: Staging archive is transient
items.content: The generated zip is a staging file. After uploads finish or fail, the wizard flow deletes it. Do not add code paths that leave staging archives behind.

items.title: Secrets never land in plan files
items.content: Backup plan JSON and backup profile files hold references only. Passwords and SAS tokens live exclusively in the KeePass-backed credential profiles.

examples.task: Add a new upload destination type
examples.decision: Implement the shared sink interface in a new Sinks.* project, wrap any vendor SDK in a matching transport project, and register the kind through dependency injection.
examples.rationale: The kind field in the plan file is data. Orchestration must not grow a switch statement for every new destination.

examples.task: Persist how many archives to keep per destination
examples.decision: Track retention in the backups.json manifest written alongside the archives at each destination.
examples.rationale: A file-based manifest travels with the data and needs no install-time infrastructure.

decisions.decision: Tests use NUnit as the runner and Shouldly for assertions, with hand-written fakes from the shared test library.
decisions.rationale: One runner and one assertion library keeps fixtures and CI reporting uniform. A second framework fragments both.

decisions.decision: Vendor storage SDK types stay behind the dedicated transport projects. Higher layers reach storage only through the shared interfaces.
decisions.rationale: Swapping or upgrading a transport should touch one place, not every layer that happens to move bytes.
constraints: storage access goes through the shared interfaces

decisions.decision: Library projects log through the Microsoft.Extensions.Logging abstractions. Concrete logger wiring lives only in the composition root.
decisions.rationale: Keeping a specific logging implementation out of the libraries lets the host decide how output is rendered and shipped.

decisions.decision: Retention state persists as a plain manifest file written next to the archives at each destination. There is no database and no object-relational mapper.
decisions.rationale: This ships as a self-contained utility. A datastore would add an install and migration burden that retention bookkeeping does not justify.
constraints: retention state stays in the manifest file

decisions.decision: Credentials live only in the KeePass-backed credential profiles under LOCALAPPDATA. Plan files and profile files carry references to them, never secret values.
decisions.rationale: Plan files get copied, committed and shared. The credential store is the one place with password protection around it.
constraints: secret values resolve at runtime from the credential store

decisions.decision: New destinations and sources are added by implementing the shared interfaces and registering the kind through dependency injection. The wizard and the orchestrator stay unaware of concrete kinds.
decisions.rationale: The kind field in the plan file is data, so adding a transport must not require touching orchestration.
constraints: new kinds register through dependency injection
